'''Anthony Gerard Martin Barrett''' is a British [[chemist]], and Sir Derek Barton Professor of Synthesis, Glaxo Professor of Organic Chemistry at [[Imperial College London]]. He is Director of the Wolfson Centre for Organic Chemistry in Medical Science.<ref>{{cite web|title=AGM Barrett Webpage|url=http://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/agm.barrett|website=Imperial College London}}</ref> He was elected a fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1999<ref>"[http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/fellows/ Fellows of the Royal Society]")</ref> and [[Academy of Medical Sciences]] in 2003.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Emeritus Professor Anthony Barrett FRS FMedSci |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/fellow/Anthony%20Gerard-Barrett-0033z00002qIIZOAA4 |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=Academy of Medical Sciences}}</ref> He obtained a BSc as well as PhD from Imperial College London in 1973 and 1975 respectively.

==Education==
Barrett was educated at [[Hele's School, Exeter|Hele's Grammar School]] in [[Exeter]]. He attended [[Imperial College, London]] (1st Class Honours BSc in 1973 and DIC and PhD in
1975). He carried out his Ph.D. working under the direction of Sir [[Derek Barton]], Nobel Laureate.

==Career and research==
Barrett was appointed lecturer in organic chemistry (1975) at IC and senior lecturer (1982). In 1983, he was appointed full professor of Chemistry at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, and in 1990 moved to Colorado State University.  After ten years research in the US, he returned to IC as Glaxo Professor of Organic Chemistry, Director of the Wolfson Centre for Organic Chemistry in Medical Science and Head of the Organic Section. He was appointed the Sir Derek Barton Professor of Synthetic Chemistry in 1999. 
Barrett has invented many reactions including novel glycosidations, atom-economic aromatic substitution reactions, metal-catalyzed oxidations and hydroaminations, reactions using ROMP-gel supported reagents and multi-component benzyne coupling reactions. He has contributed extensively to the synthesis of β-lactams using alkenyl anions, ynolates, novel isocyanates, iron vinylidines, heteroatom functionalized nitroalkenes, and ring closing alkene and enyne metathesis reactions. He has completed the total synthesis of diverse bioactive natural products including papulacandin D, papuamine, [[showdomycin]], milbemycin β3, the palmarumycins and preussomerin G,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Barrett |first1=Anthony G. A method for the deoxygenation of alcohols |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society |date=1981 |volume=Perkin Transactions |issue=1 |page=1501 |doi=10.1039/p19810001501 |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/1981/p1/p19810001501|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This not only triggered the development of thermally stable solid [[Alkalide|alkalides]]<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/ja00185a024|doi = 10.1021/ja00185a024|title = Synthesis and structures of two thermally stable sodides with the macrocyclic complexant hexamethyl hexacyclen|year = 1989|last1 = Kuchenmeister|first1 = Mark E.|last2 = Dye|first2 = James L.|journal = Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume = 111|issue = 3|pages = 935–938|url-access = subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/ja025655%2B|doi = 10.1021/ja025655+|pmid = 12022811|year = 2002|last1 = Redko|first1 = M. Y.|last2 = Vlassa|first2 = M.|last3 = Jackson|first3 = J. E.|last4 = Misiolek|first4 = A. W.|last5 = Huang|first5 = R. H.|last6 = Dye|first6 = J. L.|title = "Inverse sodium hydride": A crystalline salt that contains H(+) and Na(-)|journal = Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume = 124|issue = 21|pages = 5928–5929|url-access = subscription}}</ref> and [[Electride|electrides]]<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/ja053216f|doi=10.1021/ja053216f|title=Design and Synthesis of a Thermally Stable Organic Electride|year=2005|last1=Redko|first1=Mikhail Y.|last2=Jackson|first2=James E.|last3=Huang|first3=Rui H.|last4=Dye|first4=James L.|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=127|issue=35|pages=12416–12422|pmid=16131224|url-access=subscription}}</ref>), but also led him and his doctoral student René Riedel, in a multidisciplinary approach and in collaboration with [[Peter_Edwards_(chemist)|Peter Edwards]], to provide compelling experimental evidence for the predominant formation of alkalide [[Ion_association|ion pairs]] in solution for the first time.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi=10.1021/jacs.1c00115|title=Superalkali–Alkalide Interactions and Ion Pairing in Low-Polarity Solvents|year=2021|last1=Riedel|first1=René|last2=Seel|first2=Andrew G.|last3=Malko|first3=Daniel|last4=Miller|first4=Daniel P.|last5=Sperling|first5=Brendan T.|last6=Choi|first6=Heungjae|last7=Headen|first7=Thomas F.|last8=Zurek|first8=Eva|last9=Porch|first9=Adrian|last10=Kucernak|first10=Anthony|last11=Pyper|first11=Nicholas C.|last12=Edwards|first12=Peter P.|last13=Barrett|first13=Anthony G. M.|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=143|issue=10|pages=3934–3943|pmid=33660507|pmc=8028040}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Barrett has received numerous awards for his contributions to research from the Royal Society of Chemistry (1980 Meldola Medal,<ref>{{cite web|title= RSC Harrison-Meldola Prize|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/HarrisonMeldolaMemorialPrizes/PreviousWinners.asp|website=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref> 1982 Harrison Medal [https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/HarrisonMeldolaMemorialPrizes/], 1986 Corday-Morgan Medal [https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/CordayMorganPrizes/], 1994 Tilden Lectureship,<ref>{{cite web|title=Tilden Prize Previous Winners|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/TildenPrizes/PreviousWinners.asp|website=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref> 1996 Award in Synthetic Organic Chemistry, 2001 Award in Natural Products Chemistry, 2004 Pedler Lectureship,<ref>{{cite web|title=Pedler Award Previous Winners|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/PedlerAward/|website=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref> 2005 Simonsen Lectureship,<ref>{{cite web|title= Simonsen Award Previous Winners|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/Archive/Simonsen/|website=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref> 2010 Charles Rees Award<ref>{{cite web|title=Charles Rees Award 2010 Winner|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/CharlesReesAward/2010winner.asp|website=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref>), the American Chemical Society (1986 Cope Scholar Award), the Royal Society (2002 Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award [https://royalsociety.org/grants-schemes-awards/grants/wolfson-research-merit/]), Imperial College (1981 Armstrong Medal), the Camille and Henry Dreyfus Foundation (1987 Teacher Scholar Award [https://www.dreyfus.org/camille-dreyfus-teacher-scholar/]), Glaxo [[GlaxoSmithKline]] Wellcome (2000 Award for Innovative Chemistry), Institute of Applied Catalysis (2001 Award for Innovation in Applied Catalysis), and the Specialised Organic Sector Association (2000 Innovation Award). In 2017 he received the Imperial College President's Medal for Excellence in Research: Excellence in Innovation and Entrepreneurship [https://www.imperial.ac.uk/staff/college-staff-recognition-awards/research-excellence] (with Simak Ali, R. Charles Coombes and Matthew Fuchter).
